citation: Natesan et al., Cell Biochemistry and Biophysics (2025), doi:10.1007/s12013-025-01901-4
model: KB oral cancer cell line, 24 h exposure

insilico.note: 18 OSCC/drug-target overlaps per drug plus 25 literature genes (43 total) used for ShinyGO enrichment and STRING/CytoHubba PPI analysis.

assays.title: Cell viability (MTT)
assays.finding: Dose-dependent loss of viability; IC50 6.25 nM (DTX) and 100 µM (MTX).

assays.title: Gene expression (RT-PCR)
assays.finding: 29 genes measured. Both drugs raised BAX, CASP3, CASP9 and lowered BCL2, BRAF, MYC, ERBB2, SRC, ABCG2, RAD51, PARP1, XRCC1, MAPK1, IGIFR and PIK3CA. Several genes were drug-specific (e.g. AURKA, SLC7A5, PDGFB fall only with DTX).

assays.title: Cell migration (wound healing)
assays.finding: Migration was significantly reduced at 6 h and 24 h with both drugs.

assays.title: Colony formation
assays.finding: Colony number and surviving fraction were reduced (assay doses: DTX 0.9 nM, MTX 14.2 µM).

assays.title: DNA fragmentation
assays.finding: Enhanced DNA fragmentation (ladder) in drug-treated cells.

assays.title: Western blot
assays.finding: Increased caspases 3, 7 and 9 with both drugs.

conclusion: Authors conclude DTX showed a significantly stronger cytotoxic effect against KB oral cancer cells than MTX, with further molecular investigation warranted.
